business: Wakatta? (multilingual machine instructions with a quiz-gated machine panel, for factories employing foreign workers)
target: Owners and plant managers of small and mid-sized manufacturers in Nagasaki and Kyushu who employ 特定技能 or 技能実習 workers

segments.name: Owner-president of a small job shop (10 to 49 staff)
Plant manager at a mid-size manufacturer (50 to 299 staff)
Owner of a family firm that hired its first foreign workers this year (under 10 staff)

behaviours.name: Safety-first
behaviours.how: Has seen a near-miss involving a foreign worker and looks for anything that prevents the next one.

behaviours.name: Paper and trust
behaviours.how: Runs the shop on paper manuals, the senior worker's word and the morning meeting; distrusts new software.

behaviours.name: Leaves it to the support organisation
behaviours.how: Already pays a 登録支援機関 to handle 特定技能 support and expects them to deal with anything about it.

behaviours.name: Cost-cutter
behaviours.how: Approves only tools that cost nothing or save money they can see this quarter.

behaviours.name: Already on a tool
behaviours.how: Already uses a video-manual or checklist tool such as tebiki, Teachme Biz or カミナシ.

behaviours.name: Follows the prefecture
behaviours.how: Joins Nagasaki Prefecture or chamber of commerce programmes for foreign talent and trusts what they recommend.

behaviours.name: Lets the foremen decide
behaviours.how: Leaves floor tools to the 班長 and adopts what the foremen ask for.

objections: A tablet that locks a machine will stop production when we are busy
My foremen will not record voice notes on top of their real work
Is the Bengali or English actually right, and who is responsible if it is wrong?
Most of my foreign workers are Vietnamese or Indonesian, not Bangladeshi
We already have manuals and a support organisation for this
Free software disappears; who will support it next year?
Workers' phones, gloves and the Wi-Fi on the floor
Who sees the data about my workers' mistakes?
habits: you run the 朝礼 (morning meeting) yourself every day at 8:00
your 登録支援機関 visits once a quarter and leaves a report
you have six foreign workers and two Japanese foremen over 55
you sign the monthly safety report yourself
